facts: The Moon is visible because its surface reflects sunlight.
The Moon is Earth’s natural satellite and orbits Earth.
About how long is one lunar phase cycle?
The synodic month is about 29.5 days.
At new moon, where is the Moon roughly positioned?
At new moon the Moon is roughly between Earth and the Sun.
At full moon, which side of the Moon faces Earth?
At full moon most of the sunlit half faces Earth.
What fraction of the Moon’s disk looks lit at first quarter?
At first quarter, about half the visible disk is illuminated.
What happens after a full moon as it heads toward last quarter?
The lit portion we see decreases
The visible illuminated fraction wanes after full moon.
What does waxing mean for the Moon?
The visible lit portion is increasing
The Moon is moving away forever
Waxing means the illuminated portion we see is growing.
What does waning mean for the Moon?
The visible lit portion is decreasing
Waning means the illuminated portion we see is shrinking.
What shape describes less than half of the Moon looking lit?
A crescent phase shows less than half the disk illuminated.
What shape describes more than half but not all of the Moon looking lit?
A gibbous phase shows more than half but less than all illuminated.
Why do we usually see the same lunar face?
The Moon rotates once per orbit
Synchronous rotation keeps nearly the same face toward Earth.
What is the line between lunar day and night called?
The terminator is the boundary between light and darkness on the Moon.
Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon
The Moon blocks Earth from the Sun
A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth lies between the Sun and Moon.
The Moon blocks some sunlight from reaching Earth
Earth blocks sunlight from the Moon
A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun.
Which force links the Moon to ocean tides?
The Moon’s gravity contributes strongly to ocean tides.
Why are many Moon craters well preserved?
There is little weather and no flowing water
The Moon has almost no atmosphere and little erosion.
How thick is the Moon’s atmosphere?
The Moon has only a very tenuous exosphere.
How does lunar surface gravity compare with Earth’s?
Surface gravity on the Moon is about one sixth of Earth’s.
About how far is the Moon from Earth on average?
The average Earth–Moon distance is roughly 384,400 km.
Does the Moon’s far side always stay dark?
The far side receives sunlight too; it is simply mostly hidden from Earth.
Are normal Moon phases caused by Earth’s shadow?
Normal phases come from viewing different portions of the sunlit half.
Does the Moon rise at the same time every day?
The Moon generally rises about 50 minutes later each day on average.
Loose dust and broken rock on the surface
Regolith is the dusty, fragmented material covering much of the lunar surface.
Which mission first landed humans on the Moon?
Apollo 11 landed humans on the Moon in 1969.
